workflow: Multiple threads access an object’s shared attribute-record pointer while one thread replaces the record.
The reader loads the pointer non-atomically while the writer swaps in a replacement and releases the previous record.
The reader continues using the released record without a guaranteed live reference or synchronization.
The concurrent access becomes a data race and can dereference freed memory, terminating the process instead of safely completing the lookup.
summary: Unsynchronized shared-record replacement causes concurrent use-after-free
decision_reason: The failure workflow materially matches concurrent mutation of a shared native handle while another thread uses it without synchronization, with the released resource becoming invalid during the reader’s operation.
